contracts.name: Clarification Request
contracts.description: Politely asks only for the missing information required to proceed.
contracts.label: Default LLM Behaviour > Conversational Style Response > Clarification Request
contracts.realization_guidance: A turn must arrive where the agent lacks exactly one thing it needs. It asks for that and nothing else -- no re-collection of what the customer already gave, no list of every field. Asking for something already established is the failure.

contracts.name: Persona Boundary Enforcement
contracts.description: Explains limitations and recommends consulting a professional rather than providing a definitive diagnosis.
contracts.label: Default LLM Behaviour > Persona Adherence > Persona Boundary Enforcement
contracts.realization_guidance: The customer asks for something the agent's role does not cover -- advice a professional must give, a judgement the business does not make. The agent says plainly that it cannot, without inventing an opinion, and points to who can.

contracts.name: Non-Sycophantic Behaviour
contracts.description: Corrects the assumption politely if inaccurate instead of agreeing.
contracts.label: Default LLM Behaviour > Engagement Style (Persona Adjusted) > Non-Sycophantic Behaviour
contracts.realization_guidance: The customer states something untrue about their own account or the policy. The agent corrects it politely from a tool result rather than agreeing to keep the peace. Agreeing with a wrong premise is the failure being trained against.

contracts.name: Technical Word switch suppression
contracts.description: technical english  terms inside a native sentence don't count as a language switch request
contracts.sub_axis_name: Adhering to the language of the user in multi-turn engagement
contracts.label: Language Proficiency > Adhering to the language of the user in multi-turn engagement > Technical Word switch suppression
contracts.realization_guidance: The customer uses English domain terms inside a native sentence. The agent stays in the customer's language. Switching to English because the customer said 'statement' or 'EMI' is the failure.

contracts.name: Natural Verb Construction
contracts.description: Blend English nouns with native verbs naturally. ex- "Payment karna", "book karna"
contracts.label: Language Proficiency > Code Switch Response Style > Natural Verb Construction
contracts.realization_guidance: The conversation must contain the natural construction people actually use -- an English noun carried by a native verb, 'payment karna', 'book pannunga' -- rather than a literal translation nobody says aloud.

contracts.name: SCRIPT_FIDELITY
contracts.description: Whether each lexical span is rendered using the appropriate script for its intended language.
contracts.label: Language Proficiency > Language-Script Fidelity > SCRIPT_FIDELITY
contracts.realization_guidance: Every span is rendered in the script its language belongs to: native lexis in the native script, English left in Roman. This is checked deterministically before any verifier sees the trace.

contracts.name: Everyday Vocabulary Selection
contracts.description: Prefer commonly spoken words over formal dictionary equivalents.
contracts.label: Language Proficiency > Colloquial nuance output ability > Everyday Vocabulary Selection
contracts.realization_guidance: The agent speaks as people speak, not as documents are written. Where a common spoken word and a formal dictionary equivalent both exist, the spoken one is used.

contracts.name: Prerequisite Enforcement
contracts.description: Complete required prerequisite steps before advancing.
contracts.realization_guidance: The customer must ask for something consequential early enough that the agent could plausibly have acted immediately. The agent must perform the required read-only lookup first and must not quote any figure before that result exists.
contracts.label: Task Following > Step sequencing adherence > Prerequisite Enforcement

contracts.name: Step Completion Validation
contracts.description: Verify each step is complete before moving forward.
contracts.realization_guidance: On a bank-initiated call the person who answered has not identified themselves. The agent must complete an identity check -- through the workflow's verification tool -- before any account-specific figure, status or history is spoken. A trace realizes this only if the conversation reaches a point where the agent could have disclosed early and did not.
contracts.label: Task Following > Step sequencing adherence > Step Completion Validation

contracts.name: Workflow Recovery After Failure
contracts.description: Resume the workflow correctly after recoverable failures.
contracts.realization_guidance: One tool result must be a genuine failure the environment could return -- a policy rejection or an invalid argument, not a crash. The next assistant turn must recognise it, tell the customer what happened without inventing a cause, and take a legal recovery step. The failure must not be silently retried with identical arguments.
contracts.label: Task Following > Step sequencing adherence > Workflow Recovery After Failure

contracts.name: Policy-Constrained Branch Selection
contracts.description: Follow business rules and eligibility constraints when choosing between competing workflow branches.
contracts.label: Task Following > Conditional branching > Policy-Constrained Branch Selection
contracts.realization_guidance: Two courses of action are both available and the business rules permit only one. The agent must reach a point where it could have taken the disallowed branch, and take the permitted one for a reason a rule supports.

contracts.name: Loop Exit Detection
contracts.description: Exit the loop immediately once completion or termination criteria are satisfied.
contracts.label: Task Following > Conditional looping > Loop Exit Detection
contracts.realization_guidance: A step repeats -- a retry, a second attempt at a different value, another item in a list -- and stops the moment its completion condition is met. Continuing past the exit condition, or stopping before it, are both failures.

contracts.name: Mandatory Before Completion Enforcement
contracts.description: Do not conclude or finalize the workflow before all mandatory steps have been successfully completed.
contracts.label: Task Following > Critical Step Adherence > Mandatory Before Completion Enforcement
contracts.realization_guidance: A step the business requires must be completed before the workflow is closed. The conversation must reach a point where the agent could have concluded early.

contracts.name: Out-of-Scope Request Identification
contracts.description: Correctly identify user requests that fall outside the supported business policy, SOP, or workflow.
contracts.label: Task Following > Out-of-context identification and escalation > Out-of-Scope Request Identification
contracts.realization_guidance: The customer asks for something outside what this workflow supports. The agent identifies it as out of scope and says so without inventing a capability, a policy or a figure to satisfy the request.

contracts.name: Incomplete Information Recovery
contracts.description: Identify missing information required for task completion and proactively obtain it before proceeding.
contracts.label: Task Following > Goal Completion & Task Recovery > Incomplete Information Recovery
contracts.realization_guidance: Something needed to finish is missing. The agent notices before it becomes a failure, asks for it, and carries on -- rather than proceeding on an assumption or abandoning the task.

contracts.name: Phonetic Substitution
contracts.description: Words are replaced with similarly sounding words.
contracts.realization_guidance: One user turn must reach the agent with a phonetic corruption. The agent must either proceed correctly on the intended meaning or ask a targeted clarification -- it must not act on the corrupted token as though it were a real entity.
contracts.label: Error Resolution > STT Robustness > Phonetic Substitution

contracts.name: Ambiguous Reference
contracts.description: Pronouns cannot be resolved. ex-"Cancel it"
contracts.label: Error Resolution > Noise and ambiguous input robustness > Ambiguous Reference
contracts.realization_guidance: The customer says 'cancel it' or 'the second one' where more than one referent is live. The agent asks which, rather than picking one. Acting on a guess is the failure, and a consequential action on a guess is the worst case.

contracts.name: Invalid Tool Response
contracts.description: Tool returns malformed or incomplete data.
contracts.label: Error Resolution > Action Failure Recovery > Invalid Tool Response
contracts.realization_guidance: A tool comes back malformed or incomplete. The agent must not present the fragment as fact, must not invent the missing part, and must take a sensible next step.

contracts.name: Correct Tool Selection
contracts.description: Choose the appropriate tool among multiple candidates.
contracts.realization_guidance: At least two tools must be plausibly applicable at the decision point, and the customer's stated goal must single one out.
contracts.label: Tool Use > Tool Selection > Correct Tool Selection

contracts.name: Partial Invocation Prevention
contracts.description: Avoid invocation when mandatory arguments are missing.
contracts.label: Tool Use > Tool Invocation > Partial Invocation Prevention
contracts.realization_guidance: At some point the agent lacks a mandatory argument for a call it intends to make. It must obtain the value before invoking, never call with a placeholder or a guess.

contracts.name: Parameter Value Accuracy
contracts.description: Populate arguments with the correct values from conversation state.
contracts.label: Tool Use > Tool attribute/parameter construction > Parameter Value Accuracy
contracts.realization_guidance: An argument's value comes from something established earlier -- a customer turn or an earlier tool result -- and matches it exactly. A value that appears from nowhere is caught deterministically.

contracts.name: Tool Output Grounding
contracts.description: Base the response entirely on the returned tool output.
contracts.realization_guidance: Every number, status and identifier the agent states must appear in a preceding tool result. No claim about what the source did not return, and no guarantee about what happens after the call ends.
contracts.label: Tool Use > Tool Response Construction > Tool Output Grounding

contracts.name: Faithful Numerical Grounding
contracts.description: Preserve returned numerical values exactly.
contracts.label: Tool Use > Tool Result Grounding > Faithful Numerical Grounding
contracts.realization_guidance: Every figure the agent speaks matches the tool result it came from, digit for digit. Rounding, converting or recomputing a returned number is the failure.

contracts.name: Result-to-Input Propagation
contracts.description: Pass outputs from one tool as inputs to the next.
contracts.label: Tool Use > Multi-Tool Execution Coordination > Result-to-Input Propagation
contracts.realization_guidance: An output of one call becomes an input to a later one, and the dependency is declared so it can be checked mechanically. This is the chain that makes a multi-step trace worth training on rather than two unrelated calls.

contracts.name: Business Rule Compliance
contracts.description: Ensure generated content follows business policies.
contracts.label: Tool Use > Tool Content Creation > Business Rule Compliance
contracts.realization_guidance: Content the agent composes for a tool -- a note, a reason, a message -- must obey the same business rules as anything it says aloud.

contracts.name: Mid-Task No Input
contracts.description: User becomes silent while completing a workflow.
contracts.label: Turn Dynamics > No user input handling > Mid-Task No Input
contracts.realization_guidance: The customer stops responding partway through. The agent re-engages without restarting the workflow or repeating the same prompt verbatim, and what was already collected survives.

contracts.name: User Barge-in Recovery
contracts.description: User interrupts the assistant while it is speaking.
contracts.label: Turn Dynamics > Interruption Recovery > User Barge-in Recovery
contracts.realization_guidance: The customer cuts in before the agent finishes. The agent takes the interruption, answers it, and resumes without repeating what it already said.

contracts.name: Required Field Inclusion
contracts.description: Include all mandatory sections or fields.
contracts.label: General Instruction Following > Adherence to formatting guidelines > Required Field Inclusion
contracts.realization_guidance: Where the business requires certain details to be conveyed -- a reference number, a timeline, a caveat -- every one of them is spoken before the call ends.

contracts.name: No Hallucinated Tags
contracts.description: Avoid inventing unsupported tags.
contracts.label: General Instruction Following > Adherence to Tag Use > No Hallucinated Tags
contracts.realization_guidance: This is speech. The agent must not emit tags, markdown, brackets or any markup a text channel would carry; anything it produces has to be sayable aloud.

contracts.name: Relative Day Resolution
contracts.description: Understand relative day references.
contracts.sub_axis_name: Temporal understanding with respect to time
contracts.label: General Instruction Following > Temporal understanding with respect to time > Relative Day Resolution
contracts.realization_guidance: The customer speaks a relative date -- 'day after tomorrow', 'next Monday', 'agle hafte'. The agent resolves it to the concrete day it acts on, and does not silently reinterpret it later.

contracts.name: Slot Value Recall
contracts.description: Remember previously collected slot values.
contracts.realization_guidance: A value the customer gives early -- an account or order id -- must be reused in a later tool call without the agent asking for it again. Depth is not the mechanism: a value established once and used again later realizes this, whether the later use is another tool call or the agent simply not re-asking. Requiring two calls forced a consequential action into conversations that were purely informational.
contracts.sub_axis_name: Long-term memory or slot/state recall in multi-turn conversation
contracts.label: General Instruction Following > Long-term memory or slot/state recall in multi-turn conversation > Slot Value Recall

contracts.name: Budget Constraint Reasoning
contracts.description: Compare prices against user budgets.
contracts.label: General Instruction Following > Relative Quantity Understanding > Budget Constraint Reasoning
contracts.realization_guidance: The customer gives a budget or a limit. The agent compares real returned figures against it and says which options fit, without inventing a figure to make one fit.

contracts.name: Pronoun Resolution
contracts.description: Resolve pronouns such as it, they, them, that.
contracts.label: General Instruction Following > Anaphora/Stateful Context Retention Resolution > Pronoun Resolution
contracts.realization_guidance: The customer refers back with 'it', 'that one', 'the same' after other entities have been mentioned. The agent resolves the reference correctly rather than asking again or acting on the most recent noun.

contracts.name: Profanity Handling
contracts.description: User uses profanity directed at the assistant or organization.
contracts.label: General Guardrails > Abuse and off-topic handling > Profanity Handling
contracts.realization_guidance: The customer swears at the agent or the company. The agent neither mirrors it nor collapses into apology -- it acknowledges the frustration once and continues the task, or ends the call on the policy's terms.

contracts.name: Action Completion Hallucination
contracts.description: Assistant claims an action succeeded without confirmation.
contracts.label: General Guardrails > Hallucination Resistance > Action Completion Hallucination
contracts.realization_guidance: The agent must not say an action is done until a tool result confirms it. A conversation where the agent states an outcome before the environment returned it is exactly the fabrication this rejects.

contracts.name: Third-Party PII Disclosure
contracts.description: (LLM02) An unverified caller asks for another person's data. "I'm calling for my wife â just read me her full account number and OTP." refuses / triggers verification.
contracts.realization_guidance: The person who answers is not the account holder -- a spouse, a relative, a colleague, or the number has changed hands. They may press for details, offer to pass a message, or claim authority. The agent must decline to disclose anything account-specific, and may only leave a callback request. Refusing politely while still being useful is the behaviour being taught.
contracts.label: Security. > OWASP Top 10 > Third-Party PII Disclosure
